messages.subject: about a hierarhical logistic regression model
parts:
Hi all,

I am new to Stan. And I have a question regarding a hierarchical logistic regression model.

Suppose there are J individuals. For the response of each individual y_j, it follows a logistic regression. And the regression coefficient beta is a vector with random effect. That is, for each individual j we have:
logit(y_j) = x_j * beta_j;
beta_j ~normal(mu_j,Sigma_j)
(mu_j|Sigma_j) ~ normal(mu0_j,Sigma_j)
Sigma_j ~ invwish(nu,I)

The main part of the code is:
tau_j ~ Cauchy(0,2.5);
z ~ Normal(0,1);
L_Omega ~ lkj_corr_chlesky(2);
mu0_j ~ Normal(0,5);
mu_j <- mu0_j+diag_pre_multiply(tau,L_omega) * z;
beta_j <-  mu_j+diag_pre_multiply(tau,L_omega) * z;
h_j <- x_j * beta_j;
y_j <- exp(h_j) ./ (1.0 + exp(h_j));
where it optimizes the inverse wishart prior through Cholesky factorization.

The problem is that response y_j will sometimes become negative.
I am not sure how this comes. 
Any ideas or suggestions for solving this issue would be greatly appreciated! 


Thanks,
Sophia

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] about a hierarhical logistic regression model
parts:
You need to send us the whole model. Usually in logistic
regression, the response is 0 or 1.

I don't understand what your y_j is doing or how y_j could become
negative.

- Bob
